cohort: 64 patients in the late first stage and second stage of labour with cephalic presentation
finding: An angle of descent (AOD) of 116° or more, measured by transperineal ultrasound, was predictive of successful vaginal delivery within 2 hours.
mod_finding: The study found that a larger angle of descent, measured by transperineal ultrasound, was associated with a higher likelihood of vaginal delivery, suggesting it could be a useful tool to predict successful vaginal birth.
